docs.title: nematics Documentation
docs.text:
This repository contains a Python translation of legacy Fortran workflows for nematic liquid crystal trajectory analysis, including:

  • global orientational order parameter (S) from GRO trajectories
  • Fortran-accelerated pair-correlation analysis (5CB and CN dipole channels)
  • report plotting scripts for order and pair-correlation families

This documentation is written for two audiences:

  1. first-time users who want an exact runbook
  2. technical users who want implementation and math details

docs.title: Documentation map
docs.text:
• Quickstart: setup + first successful run
  • Workflows: reproducible command sequences for full analysis
  • CLI Reference: all commands and arguments
  • Architecture: module-level implementation map
  • Math: precise definitions and what each output column means
  • Plotting Guide: how report figures are built from generated data
  • Troubleshooting: common failure modes and fixes

docs.title: One-minute sanity check
docs.text:
source .venv-nematics/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[viz]"
nematics paf --gro-dir "<GRO_DIR>" --frame 0

If this runs and prints three eigenvalues/eigenvectors, your environment is healthy.

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
• src/nematics/gro.py: GRO parsing and frame container
  • src/nematics/paf.py: molecular axes + global PAF tensor eigensystem
  • src/nematics/order.py: trajectory-level S computation and .npy outputs
  • src/nematics/histograms.py: Fortran-style histogram data structures
  • src/nematics/paircorr.py: pair-correlation orchestration and updates
  • src/nematics/_paircorr_fort.f90: compiled inner loop for paircorr
  • src/nematics/fortran_backend.py: f2py build/load helper
  • src/nematics/cli.py: user-facing CLI

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
1. read_gro_frame(...) reads frameN.gro into positions + box.
  2. make_molecular_axes(...) derives molecular frame and dipole vectors.
  3. compute_global_paf(...) computes director from selected orientation vectors.
  4. For order: largest eigenvalue per frame is written to .npy.
  5. For paircorr: pair loops update 1D histograms with weighted channels.

docs.title: Paircorr output schema
docs.text:
Each *.dat file has shape (200, 12):

  • column 0: bin center
  • column 1: normalized counts g0-like channel
  • columns 2..11: weighted orientational channels from Fortran WW

In current plotting scripts, column 2 (WW(2) channel) is used as g1.

docs.title: Fortran acceleration design
docs.text:
Python keeps I/O and orchestration. The expensive pair+image loops are offloaded:

  • Python backend: paircorr._paircorr_update
  • Fortran backend: paircorr_fort_mod.paircorr_update

This keeps behavior identical while reducing runtime by large factors.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: The entrypoint is nematics.

docs.title: nematics paf
docs.text:
Compute PAF eigenvalues/eigenvectors for one frame.

nematics paf --gro-dir <path> [--frame 0] [--natoms-per-mol 38] [--axis molzax|ddir]

Arguments:

  • --gro-dir: directory containing frame*.gro
  • --frame: frame index (default 0)
  • --natoms-per-mol: atom count per molecule (default 38)
  • --axis: orientation set for PAF (molzax or ddir)

docs.title: nematics order
docs.text:
Compute largest eigenvalue S over all frames and default trajectory folders.

nematics order \
  [--data-root data/Poon,...] \
  [--out-dir data/order] \
  [--nframes 1000] \
  [--natoms-per-mol 38] \
  [--axis molzax|ddir] \
  [--no-progress]

docs.title: nematics paircorr
docs.text:
Compute Fortran-style pair-correlation histograms.

nematics paircorr \
  --gro-dir <path> \
  [--out-dir data/paircorr] \
  [--label <name>] \
  [--start-frame 0] \
  [--nframes 1000] \
  [--save-every 0] \
  [--natoms-per-mol 38] \
  [--backend auto|fortran|python] \
  [--auto-build-fortran] \
  [--no-progress]

Backend behavior:

  • fortran: fail if extension is unavailable
  • python: pure Python fallback
  • auto: use Fortran if available, otherwise Python

docs.title: nematics build-fortran
docs.text:
Compile pair-correlation extension module.

nematics build-fortran [--quiet]

Output:

  • shared object under src/nematics/_paircorr_fort*.so

docs.title: 1. Environment setup
docs.text:
From repo root:

uv venv .venv-nematics
source .venv-nematics/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[viz]"

If you also want documentation tooling:

uv pip install -e ".[docs]"

docs.title: 2. Set your paths
docs.text:
Define these before running commands:

  • <DATA_ROOT>: directory containing trajectory folders
  • <GRO_DIR>: one trajectory directory containing frame*.gro
  • <ORDER_DIR>: where *_S.npy files will be written
  • <PAIRCORR_DIR>: where paircorr .dat files will be written

Expected <DATA_ROOT> layout:

<DATA_ROOT>/
  gro/
  gro 2/
  gro 3/
  gro 4/

Check quickly:

ls "<GRO_DIR>/frame0.gro"

docs.title: 3. First command: single-frame PAF
docs.text:
nematics paf \
  --gro-dir "<GRO_DIR>" \
  --frame 0

docs.title: 4. Compute order arrays (for report plots)
docs.text:
nematics order --data-root "<DATA_ROOT>" --axis molzax --out-dir "<ORDER_DIR>"

This produces:

  • <ORDER_DIR>/gro_S.npy
  • <ORDER_DIR>/gro_2_S.npy
  • <ORDER_DIR>/gro_3_S.npy
  • <ORDER_DIR>/gro_4_S.npy

docs.title: 5. Build fast paircorr backend
docs.text: nematics build-fortran

docs.title: 6. Run pair correlations
docs.text:
for d in "gro" "gro 2" "gro 3" "gro 4"; do
  nematics paircorr \
    --gro-dir "<DATA_ROOT>/$d" \
    --label "${d// /_}" \
    --out-dir "<PAIRCORR_DIR>" \
    --backend fortran \
    --save-every 0
done

docs.title: 7. Generate figures
docs.text:
Order figures:

python plotting/plot_ps.py --order-dir "<ORDER_DIR>"

Paircorr figures:

python plotting/plot_paircorr.py --paircorr-dir "<PAIRCORR_DIR>" --out-dir "<REPORT_DIR>"

docs.title: Optional concrete example
docs.text:
In this repository:

  • <DATA_ROOT> = data/Poon, Chi-Duen - 5cb-x1000-gaff-88x88x94-zalign
  • <GRO_DIR> = data/Poon, Chi-Duen - 5cb-x1000-gaff-88x88x94-zalign/gro
  • <ORDER_DIR> = data/order
  • <PAIRCORR_DIR> = data/paircorr
  • <REPORT_DIR> = reports/paircorr

docs.title: 1. Order plots (plot_ps.py)
docs.text:
Command:

python plotting/plot_ps.py --order-dir "<ORDER_DIR>"

Input expected:

  • gro_S.npy
  • gro_2_S.npy
  • gro_3_S.npy
  • gro_4_S.npy

Temperature mapping in script:

  • gro_S -> 356 K
  • gro_2_S -> 366 K
  • gro_3_S -> 376 K
  • gro_4_S -> 386 K

Generated figures:

  • reports/p_s_hist.png: distribution overlays of S
  • reports/avg_s_vs_t.png: mean +/- std vs temperature

docs.title: 2. Paircorr plots (plot_paircorr.py)
docs.text:
Command:

python plotting/plot_paircorr.py --paircorr-dir "<PAIRCORR_DIR>" --out-dir "<REPORT_DIR>"

docs.title: Panels produced
docs.text:
• paircorr_5cb_along_director.png
  • paircorr_cn_along_director.png
  • paircorr_5cb_perp_radial.png
  • paircorr_cn_perp_radial.png
  • paircorr_cn_dipole_radial.png

docs.title: What is plotted now
docs.text:
plot_paircorr.py reads column 2 (W_2) from each .dat file as the plotted g1 channel.

That is:

\[ g_1 \sim \langle \mathbf{u}_i\cdot\mathbf{u}_j \rangle \]

for the species-specific orientation vectors.

docs.title: 3. If you want alternate channels
docs.text:
Edit plotting/plot_paircorr.py and change selected column index:

  • col 2: W_2 (dot product)
  • col 3: W_2^2
  • col 4: director-projected dot term
  • col 5: square of director-projected term
  • col 6: y-axis correlation

This can expose additional signatures (biaxial/tilt trends).

docs.title: zsh: command not found: nematics
docs.text:
Activate env and install editable package:

source .venv-nematics/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .

docs.title: FileNotFoundError frame0.gro
docs.text: Use absolute path or run from repo root. The CLI now attempts repo-root fallback for relative paths.

docs.title: Paircorr is very slow
docs.text:
Use Fortran backend:

nematics build-fortran
nematics paircorr ... --backend fortran --save-every 0

docs.title: Fortran backend requested but extension is not available
docs.text:
Build extension first:

nematics build-fortran

If compiler missing, install gfortran and retry.

docs.title: Matplotlib/font cache warnings
docs.text:
Set writable cache paths:

export MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/matplotlib
export XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/.cache

docs.title: plot_ps.py does not include your files
docs.text:
Ensure order filenames match expected stems:

  • gro_S.npy
  • gro_2_S.npy
  • gro_3_S.npy
  • gro_4_S.npy

*_ddir_S.npy files are intentionally separate and not used by default temperature map.

docs.title: MkDocs command not found
docs.text:
Install docs extras:

uv pip install -e ".[docs]"
mkdocs serve

docs.title: Workflow A: reproduce existing order report
docs.text:
Use this if your goal is to reproduce the current P(S) and average-S figures.

source .venv-nematics/bin/activate
nematics order --data-root "<DATA_ROOT>" --axis molzax --out-dir "<ORDER_DIR>"
python plotting/plot_ps.py --order-dir "<ORDER_DIR>"

Outputs:

  • reports/p_s_hist.png
  • reports/avg_s_vs_t.png

docs.title: Workflow B: CN-director variant
docs.text:
The 11-feb Fortran path often uses dipole-derived director context.

nematics order --data-root "<DATA_ROOT>" --axis ddir --out-dir "<ORDER_DIR>"

This writes *_ddir_S.npy files.

docs.title: Workflow C: full pair-correlation pipeline
docs.text:
nematics build-fortran
for d in "gro" "gro 2" "gro 3" "gro 4"; do
  nematics paircorr \
    --gro-dir "<DATA_ROOT>/$d" \
    --label "${d// /_}" \
    --out-dir "<PAIRCORR_DIR>" \
    --backend fortran \
    --save-every 0
done
python plotting/plot_paircorr.py --paircorr-dir "<PAIRCORR_DIR>" --out-dir "reports/paircorr"

docs.title: Workflow D: debug/smoke run (fast)
docs.text:
Use for validation before long jobs:

nematics paircorr \
  --gro-dir "<GRO_DIR>" \
  --label smoke \
  --out-dir /tmp/paircorr_smoke \
  --nframes 1 \
  --save-every 0 \
  --backend auto

docs.title: Recommended execution policy
docs.text:
• Use --backend fortran for production runs.
  • Keep --save-every 0 unless you need crash recovery checkpoints.
  • For very long jobs, run one directory at a time and archive <PAIRCORR_DIR> outputs immediately.

docs.title: Molecular orientation vectors
docs.text:
For each molecule, a unit orientation vector \(\mathbf{u}_i\) is defined from atom coordinates.

Two commonly used choices in this codebase:

  • molzax: long molecular axis
  • ddir: CN dipole direction

docs.title: Global PAF tensor
docs.text:
Given \(N\) molecules and orientation vectors \(\mathbf{u}_i=(u_{ix},u_{iy},u_{iz})\):

\[ \Omega_{\alpha\beta}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}u_{i\alpha}u_{i\beta}-\frac{N}{3}\delta_{\alpha\beta} \]

This is the traceless alignment tensor used in legacy Fortran.

Code mapping: nematics.paf.compute_global_paf.

docs.title: Eigen decomposition
docs.text:
Solve:

\[ \Omega\,\mathbf{e}_k = \lambda_k\,\mathbf{e}_k \]

Then scale eigenvalues:

\[ S_k = \frac{3}{2}\frac{\lambda_k}{N} \]

The largest scaled eigenvalue \(S_1\) is the reported nematic order parameter \(S\).

docs.title: Practical interpretation
docs.text:
• \(S\approx 1\): strong orientational alignment
  • \(S\approx 0\): weak orientational order / isotropic-like
  • negative minor eigenvalues are expected due to tracelessness

docs.title: Plot connection
docs.text:
plotting/plot_ps.py uses saved *_S.npy arrays to produce:

  • histogram \(P(S)\)
  • average \(\langle S\rangle\) vs temperature

docs.title: Math: Pair Correlations
docs.text: This page documents the pair-correlation expressions used in the report and how they map to nematics paircorr.

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text:
For a pair \((i,j)\):

  • displacement: \(\mathbf{r}_{ij} = \mathbf{r}_j - \mathbf{r}_i\)
  • global director: \(\mathbf{Z}\) (largest-eigenvector frame director)
  • parallel component: \(z_{ij} = \mathbf{r}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{Z}\)
  • perpendicular component: \(r_{\perp,ij} = \sqrt{\lVert\mathbf{r}_{ij}\rVert^2 - z_{ij}^2}\)

Periodic boundary conditions are handled with 27 image shifts \((k_x,k_y,k_z)\in\{-1,0,1\}^3\).

docs.title: Parallel family (cylindrical selection)
docs.text:
For a cylinder radius \(R\):

\[ g_{0,\parallel}(z;R) \propto \left\langle \delta\!\left(z-\mathbf{r}_{ij}\!\cdot\!\mathbf{Z}\right)\, \Theta\!\left(R^2-r_{\perp,ij}^2\right) \right\rangle_{ij} \]

Orientational channel (used as \(g_1\) in plotting):

\[ g_{1,\parallel}(z;R) \propto \left\langle \left(\mathbf{u}_i\!\cdot\!\mathbf{u}_j\right)\, \delta\!\left(z-\mathbf{r}_{ij}\!\cdot\!\mathbf{Z}\right)\, \Theta\!\left(R^2-r_{\perp,ij}^2\right) \right\rangle_{ij} \]

docs.title: Perpendicular family (thin slab around director plane)
docs.text:
For slab half-thickness \(d_z\):

\[ g_{0,\perp}(r_\perp;d_z) \propto \left\langle \delta\!\left(r_\perp-r_{\perp,ij}\right)\, \Theta\!\left(d_z-\lvert z_{ij}\rvert\right) \right\rangle_{ij} \] \[ g_{1,\perp}(r_\perp;d_z) \propto \left\langle \left(\mathbf{u}_i\!\cdot\!\mathbf{u}_j\right)\, \delta\!\left(r_\perp-r_{\perp,ij}\right)\, \Theta\!\left(d_z-\lvert z_{ij}\rvert\right) \right\rangle_{ij} \]

docs.title: Radial family
docs.text:
\[ r_{ij}=\lVert\mathbf{r}_{ij}\rVert \] \[ g_{0,\mathrm{rad}}(r) \propto \left\langle \delta\!\left(r-r_{ij}\right) \right\rangle_{ij}, \qquad g_{1,\mathrm{rad}}(r) \propto \left\langle \left(\mathbf{u}_i\!\cdot\!\mathbf{u}_j\right)\, \delta\!\left(r-r_{ij}\right) \right\rangle_{ij} \]

In code these are discretized in bins and normalized with geometry-dependent factors (dnz, dnr, dnr2).

docs.title: Weighted channels (Fortran WW)
docs.text:
For each accepted pair, channels are:

\[ \begin{aligned} W_1 &= 1 \\ W_2 &= \mathbf{u}_i\cdot\mathbf{u}_j \\ W_3 &= (W_2)^2 \\ W_4 &= (\mathbf{u}_i\cdot\mathbf{Z})(\mathbf{u}_j\cdot\mathbf{Z}) \\ W_5 &= (W_4)^2 \\ W_6 &= \mathbf{y}_i\cdot\mathbf{y}_j \end{aligned} \]

Species definition:

  • 5CB: \(\mathbf{u}\) is molecular long axis (molzax)
  • CN: \(\mathbf{u}\) is dipole direction (ddir)

docs.title: Histogram families written by the code
docs.text:
• par_1.0, par_2.0, par_3.0, par_all: bins in \(|z|\) with \(r_\perp<R\), \(R\in\{1,2,3,5\}\) nm
  • per: bins in \(r_\perp\) with \(|z|<d_z\), \(d_z=0.2\) nm
  • rad: bins in \(r\)
  • default binning: 200 bins over \([0,5]\) nm

docs.title: Output columns in each .dat file
docs.text:
• col 0: bin center
  • col 1: baseline count channel (\(g_0\)-like)
  • col 2: \(W_2\) channel (used as g1 in current plotting)
  • col 3: \(W_3\)
  • col 4: \(W_4\)
  • col 5: \(W_5\)
  • col 6: \(W_6\)
  • col 7..11: reserved (currently zero with ylen=10)

docs.title: Plot mapping
docs.text: plotting/plot_paircorr.py currently plots col 2 for all panels, so those curves are the \(W_2\) orientational-correlation channel.
